newsitem.title: UK: MAM takes major Alliance & Leicester stake.
newsitem.headline: MAM takes major Alliance & Leicester stake.

text.p: Mercury Asset Management Plc, one of the UK's biggest fund managers, has built up a stake of over six percent in recently-floted banking group Alliance & Leicester Plc, according to a research group.

Citywatch, a research house which specialises in analysing the ownership of UK public companies, said MAM had acquired a stake of at least 6.26 percent, though its research covered only 52 percent of the shares in issue and MAM's actual stake was likely to be higher.

The size of MAM's stake, which makes it the biggest single shareholder in the former mutually-owned group, has not been officially announced but could be a significant factor in A&L's life as a publicly-quoted firm, analysts and traders said.
A&L is formally protected from takeover for five years unless it buys another financial institution or 75 percent of its shareholders vote to waive its immunity.

Other institutional shareholders held stakes of less than two percent, Citywatch said. Alliance and Leicester said it was not aware of any specific large shareholdings that had been built up, but it would not be surprised to see MAM holding a large stake.
"It is significant because clearly you have to feel that taking a stake that large in any company is more than just a normal portfolio investment," said one analyst, who asked not to be named.

"And it is in a company that by virtue of its (relatively small) size would be seen as a key takeover play in the sector...it sounds as if they believe either something is going to happen or that the rumours of something happening will make it a good investment."

He pointed out that MAM's stake meant it had some 20 percent of freely available A&L shares, or those which had not been retained by its former owners. "It could put them (MAM) in a prime position to control events," the analyst said.
After hectic trading as A&L shares made a storming market debut on April 21, the shares have held near their peaks well above the levels analysts originally had expected.

The strength of the stock's performance after its debut took the market by surprise, with a shortage of stock leaving investment funds scrambling to build up a position in the company which is expected to join the FTSE 100 index next month.

The stock's sharp rise also reverberated through the rest of the bank sector, with traders and investors drawing the conclusion that Halifax and Woolwich would also perform well -- prompting renewed buying in existing banks as investors aimed to increase their weighting to reflect the sector's growing size.
Dealers said the MAM stake was an intriguing fresh development since the flotation.
"It is a strategic stake," said one, "if anyone would want to make a bid, the first thing they would do would be to knock on MAM's door."
A&L shares on Thursday closed down 1/2p at 572-1/2 in volume of 2.5 million shares.

Citywatch pointed out that MAM's position in A&L is well above its holding of some 2.9 percent in UK retail banks as a whole. Overall the fund manager holds 3.8 percent of the UK equity market, Citywatch said.
No-one at MAM was immediately available for comment.
